title: Buick Skylark Engines by Year (1953–1998)
description: Every factory engine in the Buick Skylark and Gran Sport by year, 1953–1998: the Nailhead, aluminum 215, GS 400 and 455 Stage 1, and later V6s and fours.
intro: Buick used the Skylark name on a 1953–1954 luxury convertible, on its compact and mid-size cars from 1961 to 1972, and on smaller Buicks through 1998. The Gran Sport, a Skylark-based performance model, carried Buick's largest engines; the trims column shows which ones.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The original Skylark was a limited-production convertible with Buick's 322 Nailhead V8.
The compact Skylark used Buick's aluminum 215 V8.

The mid-size Skylark moved to cast-iron V8s: the 300, 340 and 350, with the 401 Nailhead, 400 and 455 reserved for the Gran Sport. The 455 Stage 1 was the top engine from 1970. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The compact rear-drive Skylark used Buick's 231 V6 and V8s built by Buick, Oldsmobile, Pontiac and Chevrolet; the notes say which.
From 1980 the Skylark was front-drive, with GM fours and V6s: the 2.5, the 2.8, Buick's 3.0 and 3.3, Oldsmobile's Quad 4 and 2.4, and the 3100.

notes.1969|400|345: Stage 1. Published ratings for this engine vary.
